capabilities.local_comparison: Compare two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon with exactly one adopted weight change. Measures local plan/endpoint differences; does not establish closed-loop settling or causal attribution. Requires a saved effective horizon matching the authorized horizon.
capabilities.prediction_braking: At one saved projected state, compare recorded input with instantaneous braking-box input over the fixed short horizon. Can measure local endpoint speed/position differences. Cannot separate objective weighting, seed selection, horizon effects or backend-model mismatch when they predict the same result; cannot identify the dominant settling cause.

discriminating_observations: Endpoint tip speed difference (m/s) between the recorded-input rollout and the braking-box rollout at the same saved state: a difference beyond 0.02 m/s supports H1; a difference within that scale supports H2.
Endpoint tip position difference (m) between the two rollouts: a difference beyond 0.01 m supports H1; a difference within that scale supports H2.
Sign/direction of the endpoint speed change (whether the braking-box arm lowers endpoint speed relative to the recorded arm), reported as a local measurement only.
hypotheses: H1 (local input sensitivity): at update 34's saved projected GVS state, over the fixed 0.01 s implicit-Euler horizon the held recorded applied tension (/34/actual_tension_n = [3.1758909392099772, 2.757372796476204, 1.4216485070827969e-08, 0.8929758192138912, 0.12734806870748366, -0.0] N, all within the 8 N per-channel limits) and an instantaneous braking-box input predict materially different local endpoints (endpoint tip speed differs by more than 0.02 m/s or endpoint tip position by more than 0.01 m), so the applied input is locally separable at the 10 ms scale.

H2 (local input insensitivity): the two inputs predict effectively the same local endpoint over 0.01 s, because the saved projected state and short horizon dominate; in that case objective_weighting, seed_or_iteration_plan_selection, horizon_or_deadline_effects and backend_model_mismatch all predict the same local result and this check cannot separate them at all.

request_content.question: Open diagnostic question (no root cause presumed): Why does secondary settling performance fail while terminal reach succeeds? In the bound summary, reach passes (terminal_error_m = 0.007642608585867386 < reach_tolerance_m 0.01, reach_passed true), yet the sampled settling window fails (sampled_settling_passed false; late_max_speed_m_s = 1.5810152739742807 and late_max_error_m = 0.05813810428573256 against speed_limit_m_s 0.02, position_limit_m 0.01, window_s 0.05; terminal_speed_m_s = 0.6351726092425104). Which observable differences are actually separable within the retained evidence and the authorized bounded checks — specifically (a) recorded applied tension versus an instantaneous braking-box input at the same saved projected state over the fixed short horizon, and (b) two local controller solves at the same saved state/previous input/horizon differing by exactly one adopted weight — and which candidate explanations (objective weighting, seed/iteration selection, horizon or deadline effects, backend-model mismatch) remain mutually indistinguishable with these tools? The question is deliberately open about direction; it asks what can be distinguished, not what is already known to be the cause.
